claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A computational method combining machine learning, first-principles calculations, and CALPHAD would be more efficient than current computational approaches.
The proposed combined method can accurately predict Young's modulus of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed combined method can accurately predict yield strength of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed combined method can accurately predict toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, machine learning, and thermophysical or phenomenological parameters are established approaches for screening or characterizing high-entropy alloys.
First-principles and related atomistic calculations are computationally demanding and difficult to use for high-throughput alloy discovery.
CALPHAD can require substantial computational resources and may be limited by inadequate high-entropy-alloy databases.
Direct prediction of fracture and yield behavior is largely beyond currently available DFT implementations.
Machine-learning methods can accelerate alloy discovery but depend on the size and composition of their training data.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations act as a structural mediator linking the computational intervention to predicted mechanical properties.
Combining the three modeling approaches improves both computational efficiency and predictive accuracy through novel methods or potentials.
The method should be evaluated prospectively and blindly against tensile and fracture-test measurements.
Failure to predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness within 10% of experimental values would falsify the hypothesis.
